title: Table, graph and roots for y = x^2 - 5x + 3

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2019). In part (b) the printed inequality is the closed interval from -1 to 6 inclusive. Official answers and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The printed grid is not reproduced. All three parts are paper/self-mark: (a) is a set of three table values (MS: 2 marks, B1 for two correct); (b) requires a drawn curve; (c) is a graph reading, FT the curve, official ranges 0.6 to 0.8 and 4.2 to 4.4.

stem:
This question is 0580/32/O/N/19 Question 6, taken from the official QP.

(a) Complete the table of values for \(y=x^2-5x+3\).

The \(x\)-values are \(-1\), \(0\), \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(5\), \(6\). The given \(y\)-values are: when \(x=1\), \(y=-1\); when \(x=2\), \(y=-3\); when \(x=3\), \(y=-3\); when \(x=4\), \(y=-1\); when \(x=5\), \(y=3\). The missing values are those for \(x=-1\), \(x=0\) and \(x=6\).

(b) On a grid, draw the graph of \(y=x^2-5x+3\) for \(-1\leqslant x\leqslant 6\).

(c) Use your graph to solve the equation \(x^2-5x+3=0\).

steps.name: T2
steps.note: The third table value; official scheme awards B1 if two of the three are correct, and 2 marks if all three are correct. Official answer (a): 9, 3, 9.

steps.name: C
steps.text_tex: (b) Plot the points from the completed table and join them with a smooth symmetrical curve.
steps.note: MS: Correct curve, 4 marks; B3FT for 7 or 8 correctly plotted points, or B2FT for 5 or 6, or B1FT for 3 or 4. Official answer (b): Correct curve.

steps.name: R1
steps.text_tex: (c) The smaller root from the graph is between \(0.6\) and \(0.8\).
steps.note: MS: 0.6 to 0.8, FT their curve, B1 for each.

steps.name: R2
steps.text_tex: The larger root from the graph is between \(4.2\) and \(4.4\).
steps.note: MS: 4.2 to 4.4, FT their curve, B1 for each. Official answer (c): 0.6 to 0.8, 4.2 to 4.4.
